items.description: The only source is the image in Table 1's 'Boundary Conditions' column. The text never gives the 2-D height-to-length ratio. It says only that the longest side is normalised to 1 mm (Sec. 4.5) and that the case is 'similar' to NTopo's 2-D cantilever (Sec. 4.1). The Table 1 compliance magnitudes cannot settle it, because thickness and the compliance definition are also unspecified.

The supports are shown only in the Table 1 image. The word 'cantilever' and the whole-side hard constraint of Sec. 3.2.1 (a function of c_x only, zero along the entire side c_x = −0.5) suggest a fully clamped short end. However, the text never states which edge is fixed or how much of it is fixed for this example.
readings: entire left edge (x = 0, 0 ≤ y ≤ H) clamped, u_x = u_y = 0
only a segment of the left edge clamped (e.g. H/3 ≤ y ≤ 2H/3)

items.entity: end load on the free (right) edge
items.description: The load point appears only in the Table 1 image. The paper's other cantilevers use both a bottom-end load (Table 3, 'right bottom end loaded') and an end-face centre load (Fig. 5), so neither can be assumed here.
readings: x = L, y = 0 (bottom-right corner; top-right corner is mirror-equivalent)
x = L, y = 0.5H (mid-height of the right edge)

items.description: The direction of the end load is never stated for this example and is shown only in the Table 1 image. 'Cantilever beam' implies a transverse (vertical) load. For a single load, reversing its sign changes neither the compliance nor the layout.

Eq. 5 applies the load as a traction T over an area A, sampled at N_b boundary points. Sec. 4.5 refers to 'force vector location points'. The loaded length for this 2-D case is never given. It is also not stated whether the FE/SIMP model uses a nodal point force or a traction over a patch.
readings: concentrated force of 0.1 N at a single FE node
uniform traction totalling 0.1 N over a short edge segment (about 1–3 elements, a few % of H) at the load point

items.description: Eq. 4 is stated only 'for 3d problems'. For the 2-D example the text gives no plane-stress or plane-strain assumption and no out-of-plane thickness. Yet E = 1000 N/mm², ν = 0.3 and F = 0.1 N (Sec. 4.5) are 3-D quantities. Thickness scales compliance by 1/t. The stress-state choice changes the effective modulus and Poisson's ratio.
readings: plane stress, unit thickness t = 1 mm
plane strain (unit depth), i.e. Eq. 4 with 3-D Lamé constants applied to in-plane strains

items.description: Sec. 3.3 gives E = E_material·ρ³ with ρ from a sigmoid, so there is no lower bound. No E_min or ρ_min is stated for the SIMP run, for the FEA re-evaluation of DMF-TONN designs, or for the thresholded designs (Sec. 4, 4.1).

items.entity: 2-D structured FE/SIMP grid (also DMF-TONN volume and evaluation grid)
items.description: No 2-D grid is given; only 3-D grids such as 40×20×8 are stated (Sec. 4.2). This grid defines the SIMP design variables, the constant grid for DMF-TONN's volume term (Sec. 4.5), and the FE grid on which all Table 1 compliances are evaluated (Sec. 4). Sec. 4.6 says only that SIMP grids always have more than 6000 points.
readings: coarser 60 × 30 or 100 × 50 if the >6000-point rule is not meant for the 2-D case

items.description: Sec. 4 states a density filter with radius 1.5 × element size 'in each of the presented examples'. Because the 2-D mesh is unknown, the physical radius, which controls member size and count, is undetermined. It is also unclear whether to keep 1.5 elements or a fixed physical radius on a different mesh.
readings: r_min = 1.5 elements of the adopted mesh (e.g. 1.5/120 mm ≈ 0.0125 mm for 120 elements along L)

items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only that the cited 88-line SIMP code was run 'with the default convergence criterion'. The text gives no tolerance, iteration cap or OC parameters. The values 200 iterations and 0.01 tolerance are stated only for Top3D (Sec. 4.4).
readings: OC update, move limit 0.2, stop when the maximum design change is below 0.01, no iteration cap
same 0.01 tolerance but capped at 200 iterations

items.entity: DMF-TONN Fourier-feature kernel for 2-D (its implicit length-scale control)
items.description: The kernel settings in Sec. 4.5 are for 3-D: '16 in all three directions' with bounds ±35, or a 24/12 grid with ±45 for skewed domains. No 2-D values are given, although Sec. 3.1 says the kernel range controls feature frequency. This matters only for reproducing the DMF-TONN column of Table 1.
readings: 24 × 12 kernel grid, bounds ±45 (if the domain is ≥3:1)

items.entity: number of DMF-TONN optimisation iterations n_opt
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives n_opt = 2000 for this 2-D problem. Sec. 4.2 says n_opt = 700 is used 'for each of the presented examples in this paper' and that later iterations refine the topology.

Sec. 3.3 and line 19 of Algorithm 1 call the internal strain energy (½uᵀKu) the 'compliance'. The Table 1 values are instead 'FEA compliance' from the SIMP solver (Sec. 4), which the text does not define and is conventionally Fᵀu = 2 × strain energy.

Sec. 4.1 says only that designs are thresholded 'ensuring the volume fraction remains the same'. The text does not say which field is thresholded: filtered or raw SIMP densities, and whether DMF-TONN is sampled at SIMP-grid element centres. The cut-off rule and the void stiffness used in the binary FE analysis are also not given.
readings: threshold filtered (physical) element densities so exactly 50% of SIMP-grid elements are solid; voids = E_min
threshold raw (unfiltered) design variables at the 50%-volume cut-off; voids = E_min
remove voids entirely and analyse only the solid elements

locator: Sec. 4.1, the 2-D cantilever beam of Table 1
